Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the quick turn on the SIG. A couple of follow-ups from our security team on the incident response section:

1) Notification window: Do you commit to an initial customer notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident? If not, what is the expected maximum window and what factors might extend it?
2) Contacts & handover: We need a primary POC and a secondary on-call for legal/notification coordination. Can you provide names, roles, and escalation order?
3) Evidence escrow: For procurement we need to understand how evidence (logs, timelines) can be made available for review — timeline and format, and whether there is an option for a read-only escrow during an active incident.

Would love a short note with concrete timelines and named contacts so we can close the SIG items. We may need a lightweight addendum for procurement language depending on answers.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Information Security Lead
BrightLens, Inc.

Hi Alicia —

Thanks — answers below, plus a proposed short-timesheet we can sign off on. Attaching a compact playbook and a contact spreadsheet (SIG_IR_Contacts.xlsx, IR_Notification_Playbook.pdf). Also attaching our SOC 2 summary for context.

1) Notification window: Our standard policy is: initial acknowledgement to the customer within 24 hours of confirmation that an incident impacts customer data or production availability; initial detailed notification (what we know, affected surface, immediate mitigations) within 72 hours of confirmation. Exceptions: (a) active criminal investigation where law enforcement requests delay, (b) incidents requiring cross-customer correlation that require additional time to verify scope. In any exception we notify the customer that the timeline is extended and provide regular status updates.

2) Contacts & handover: primary POC for notification and coordination: Vivek Kulkarni (Director, Security Operations) — vivek@redwood.inference — mobile +1-415-555-0133. Secondary/on-call escalation: Neha Kapoor (Head of Compliance) — neha@redwood.inference. Legal engagement: Laura Bennett (VP Legal) — laura@redwood.inference. The spreadsheet lists escalation order and alternate contacts (security rota). If you prefer we can provide a signed contact attestation for procurement.

3) Evidence escrow & logs: we can provide time-bounded exports of relevant logs (structured JSON/CSV) and a timeline summary within 7 business days after incident confirmation for standard incidents; for high-severity incidents where customers require deeper review we offer a controlled, read-only evidence escrow for up to 90 days, subject to NDA and an access request process. We do not provide raw disk images by default; any request for that route is handled case-by-case.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm the contact sheet entries and whether BrightLens wants the evidence escrow option in procurement language (we can add a clause).
- If agreed, I can share a one-page addendum and we can loop legal for signature.

I will leave Vivek/Neha to add any operational specifics.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Head of Security Programs (acting)
Redwood Inference

Alicia — quick operational clarifications from my side:

- "Confirmation" in our policy means we have evidence of a security event that affects production systems or customer data. That may be internal detection or an external report. The 24/72 windows start at that confirmation timestamp.
- Escalation path: Security Triage -> Incident Manager -> Customer Notification -> Legal/Compliance -> Exec escalation. We try to keep the exec escalation to incidents with cross-customer impact or material data exfiltration.
- Playbook excerpts (from attached): initial triage checklist takes up to 4 hours; scope determination up to 24 hours; timeline summary delivered within 72 hours.

On evidence: for the read-only escrow we provision an S3 bucket with restricted IAM and short-lived credentials specifically for the review team; audit logs of access are recorded and shared. Normal turnaround for packaging logs is 5–7 business days. If BrightLens needs a continuous streaming export (for high-sensitivity customers) we can propose a separate commercial arrangement.

Happy to hop on 30 min if you want to walk the playbook.

 - Vivek
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Alicia / team — additional compliance notes:

- We maintain SOC 2 Type II and provide report summaries on request under NDA; full SOC 2 reports are available to customers after an executed non-disclosure agreement or via our secure report portal.
- Evidence retention: logs used for incident investigation are retained for 180 days in our standard plan; we can extend retention for customers on Dedicated plans or via contract.
- If procurement wants specific contract language around notification timelines, suggest the following concise clause: "Supplier will notify Customer of any confirmed incident impacting Customer Data within 72 hours of confirmation and provide regular updates until remediation." We're open to including the standard exceptions (law enforcement, cross-customer correlation).

I'll prepare a short procurement-friendly addendum and share a draft by EOD tomorrow if you want.

Regards,
